note: Desired archive schema — every field the spec decided that `master` does not have.
AWK-30. Read by migrate_schema.py, asserted by archive-schema.test.ts.
Each entry under `addFields` is a VERBATIM Contentful field object, so the
applier appends it as-is and never translates. Anything that is not a field
object lives at the group level, outside them.
ADDITIVE ONLY. Nothing here removes or retypes a field. The two destructive
changes the spec calls for are deliberately absent:
* `work.genre` is NOT deleted. ADR-0007 retires it, but only after the
genre -> forms data migration (AWK-37). Deleting it here would drop 218
assignments with nothing to migrate from.
* `work.slug`'s `unique: true` is NOT removed by a default run. See `gated`.
`work.slug` itself already exists and is repurposed in place, not added, so

period: IMSLP's nine values, adopted verbatim and untranslated — ADR-0007.
`Early 20th century` is IMSLP's own casing. Capitalising `Century` would
silently break the seed match in AWK-37, which compares against the wiki's
forms: 25 values: the 17 existing `genre` entry names, plus the 8 additions
ADR-0007 names for the 104 uncategorised works — Tone Poem, Dance,
Song cycle, Oratorio, Excerpt, Capriccio, Chamber work, Film music.
Merged and sorted alphabetically so the list diffs cleanly and reads as one
vocabulary rather than two eras. Casing is ADR-0007's verbatim: `Song cycle`,
`Chamber work` and `Film music` really do carry a lowercase second word
`Aria` is kept even though ADR-0007 shows the live bucket is mostly
mislabelled excerpts — about four of the thirteen are genuine arias, and
`Excerpt` now exists to take the rest. The bucket was wrong, not the word.
Extending this vocabulary later means editing this `in` list and re-running
the applier. There is no `genre` entry to create any more.
orchestras: AWK-59. An ARRAY, not a single Link, and the array is the whole point.
Seasons 1-52 are one continuous numbering carried by one institution across
two renamings -- Brooklyn Heights Music Society, then Brooklyn Heights
Orchestra, then Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra. One Season straddles a renaming
mid-season and is held by two orchestras:
* Season 5 opens at BHMS on 1977-10-25, continues at BHO from 1977-12-17
A single Link would put a false value on it. Splitting it into two entries
would invent a Season that never happened and break the 1-52 run.
Season 28 LOOKS like a second case against the live space, and is not. Its
2001-05-24 concert is linked there to BSO, against the spreadsheet, against
the entry's own title, and against participation-checklist.md. Alex settled
it on 2026-08-29: the link is wrong, Season 28 is wholly BHO, and the BSO
name begins at Season 29. See `knownLiveErrors` in season-orchestras.json.
This field does NOT make a Season identifiable on its own. The invariant the
data needs is (institution, number), which Contentful cannot express -- it
offers space-wide uniqueness only, the same wall ADR-0008 hit with
(composer, slug). It is enforced in season-orchestras.test.ts, off the build
path, because ADR-0006 keeps `season` out of loadArchive() entirely.
arrangementType: ADR-0005's four verbs, matching what the source actually writes:
arr. on 24 records, orch. on 10, trans. on 1, ed. on 1.

why: AWK-59. `season.number` carries `unique: true`, and the invariant the data
actually needs is (institution, number) -- which is composite, which
Contentful cannot express. The same wall ADR-0008 hit with (composer, slug).
The Long Island Youth Orchestra's 29th season and the Brooklyn lineage's
29th season are both genuinely season 29. Neither number is wrong, so
renumbering one to satisfy a space-wide constraint would record something
false. The constraint is what has to give.
SYMPTOM: a draft saves fine and PUBLISHING fails with `There's already an
entry with the same field value.` Unique is enforced at publish time
against published entries only, so the collision is invisible until the
moment you try to publish -- and never resolves on its own, because the
entry it collides with stays published.
ORDERING, per ADR-0008: the assertion comes first. It already exists --
season-orchestras.test.ts asserts that (institution, number) is unique AND
that `number` alone is not, so the constraint being dropped here is
replaced rather than abandoned. That test does NOT run in the build:
ADR-0006 keeps `season` out of loadArchive(), and AWK-59 chose script-side
enforcement deliberately.
`season.label` KEEPS its `unique: true`. It is the stronger guard of the
two -- it is what stops two seasons reading identically in an entry picker,
which is the problem AWK-59 opened with.
ADR-0008 removes `unique: true` from `work.slug` because the invariant the
URL scheme needs is `(composer, slug)`, which is composer-scoped, and
Contentful can only express space-wide uniqueness. 9 title families collide
globally across 20 records, so the space-wide constraint is what forced the
importer to hash in the first place.
But ADR-0008 is equally explicit that the build assertion must be written
FIRST: 'Otherwise there is a window in which nothing protects the invariant
at all.' That assertion is AWK-39, which AWK-30 blocks — so a default run of
this script cannot satisfy the ordering, and does not try.
Run this step only once AWK-39's `(composer, slug)` assertion is in the
build and passing. Until then `unique: true` is the only thing standing
between the space and 20 silently-colliding work slugs.
